title: Waves in air, fluids and solids: Reflection of waves (physics only)

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Diffuse reflection
items.clue: Reflection from a rough surface, such as paper or a painted wall.

items.label: Specular reflection
items.clue: Reflection from a smooth surface, such as a plane mirror or still water.

items.label: Transmission
items.clue: The process in which a wave passes through the boundary and continues to travel inside the second material.

items.label: Normal
items.clue: The construction line drawn at right angles to the surface at the point where the ray meets it, shown dashed in a ray diagram.

questions.stem: A sound wave travelling through the air reaches a thick concrete wall. Which statement best describes reflection at this boundary?

options.text: Some of the sound is sent back into the air it originally came from
Reflection cannot occur here, as concrete is not polished
All of the sound must pass on into the concrete and travel through
The wall turns the sound into a wave of a much higher frequency

questions.explanation: Reflection at a boundary sends part of the wave back into the first material, and air and concrete are two different materials.

questions.stem: A lamp lights a plane mirror and a sheet of white paper equally. A clear image is seen in the mirror but not in the paper. Why is this?

options.text: The rough paper scatters rays and so breaks the law of reflection
The paper absorbs every ray of light that arrives at it
The smooth mirror keeps parallel rays parallel when they reflect
Paper transmits light, but a mirror is unable to transmit

questions.explanation: Specular reflection at a smooth surface preserves the pattern of the rays so an image forms, whereas the rough paper scatters them.

questions.stem: A radio wave meets a thick metal sheet and is absorbed. What happens to the energy that the wave was carrying?

options.text: It is destroyed, so less energy exists than there was before
It is transferred to the thermal energy store of the metal
It is stored inside the wave until that wave is set free again
It becomes a reflected wave of exactly the same frequency

questions.explanation: Absorption transfers the energy carried by the wave into the energy stores of the material, most often the thermal store.

questions.stem: Light from a street lamp shines on a clean window and carries on into the room beyond. Which word describes what the light has done at the glass?

options.text: The light has been absorbed by glass
The light has been reflected away
The light has been fully destroyed
The light has been transmitted

questions.explanation: Transmission is a wave passing through the boundary and continuing to travel inside the second material.

questions.stem: A narrow ray of light travels through air and meets the flat surface of a glass block. Which statement about this boundary is correct?

options.text: All the light is transmitted, because the glass is transparent
All the light is absorbed, since the glass warms up a little
Some light is transmitted into the glass and some is reflected back
None of the light gets in until the angle reaches ninety degrees

questions.explanation: In general all three effects occur together, and a faint reflected ray is visible alongside the much brighter transmitted one.

questions.stem: You are drawing a ray diagram for light reflecting from a plane mirror. From which line is the angle of incidence measured?

options.text: From the normal, drawn at right angles to the mirror surface
From the mirror surface, at the point where the ray lands on it
From the flat surface, along where the ray hits it
From the bottom edge of the paper the diagram sits on

questions.explanation: Angles of incidence and reflection are always measured between the ray and the normal at the point of incidence.

questions.stem: A ray strikes a plane mirror at an angle of incidence of 30°. What is the angle of reflection, and from where is it measured?

options.text: 60°, measured from the normal, since they total 90°
30°, measured from the surface of the mirror
60°, measured from the mirror surface, not the normal
30°, measured from the normal on its other side

questions.explanation: The law of reflection gives angle of reflection = angle of incidence, with both angles measured from the normal.

questions.stem: Which feature must appear in a correctly drawn ray diagram showing reflection at a plane mirror?

options.text: A dashed normal drawn along the mirror surface
Arrows on the rays to show the direction
The image marked in front of the mirror surface
An angle of reflection larger than incidence

questions.explanation: Rays are drawn as straight lines carrying arrows, so the diagram shows which way the light is travelling.

questions.stem: A matt black metal plate and a shiny silver metal plate are left side by side in bright sunlight. Why does the black plate become hotter?

options.text: It reflects more of the light, and reflection is what warms a surface
The silver plate reflects all the light, so it absorbs none and cannot warm up
The silver plate absorbs the light but re-emits all of it at once
It absorbs more of the light, transferring that energy to its thermal store

questions.explanation: Absorption at the interface transfers the energy of the wave into the material and raises its temperature; reflected energy leaves again.

questions.stem: Heavy fabric curtains are drawn across a window facing a busy road, and the room becomes noticeably quieter. Which effect best explains this?

options.text: The curtain reflects all the sound waves straight back
The soft fabric absorbs much of the sound that reaches it
The curtain bounces the noise straight back outdoors
The curtain slows the sound so it arrives too late to hear

questions.explanation: Soft porous materials absorb sound, transferring the energy of the wave to their thermal energy store, so less is transmitted into the room.

questions.stem: In Required practical activity 9 a ray box is aimed at a plane mirror, then at gloss card, then at matt card. Which quantity must be kept the same throughout?

options.text: The angle of incidence of the ray from the box
The kind of surface that the ray box is aimed at
The surface type placed in front of the ray box
The sharpness of the reflected ray on paper

questions.explanation: The type of surface is the independent variable, so the angle of incidence is the control variable and must be held constant.

questions.stem: In Required practical activity 9 a ray of light is shone from air into a rectangular glass block, meeting the surface at an angle to the normal. What is seen as the ray enters the block?

options.text: It bends away from the normal
It carries straight on, unbent
It bends towards the normal
It spreads out and bends away from the normal

questions.explanation: Light slows on entering glass, so a ray meeting the surface at an angle to the normal is refracted towards the normal.
